## Key ideas {#ss2-key-ideas .series-key-ideas}

::: {.series-summary-row}
<h3>Partial sum</h3>

$$S_n=\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n}a_k=a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n$$
:::

::: {.series-summary-row}
<h3>Summation (sigma) notation</h3>

$$\sum\limits_{n=p}^{q}a_n=\underbrace{a_p+a_{p+1}+\cdots+a_q}_{q-p+1\text{ terms}}\qquad(1\le p\le q)$$
:::

::: {.series-summary-row}
<h3>Recovering a term</h3>

$$a_1=S_1\qquad a_n=S_n-S_{n-1}\quad(n\ge2)$$
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 9 · Complete your Key Ideas box.</p>

::: notes
Use the equations to summarise the lesson. In the first line n is the number of terms and k is the summation index. In the second line n is the summation index and p,q are positive integer bounds. Summation notation and sigma notation name the same notation. Both bounds are included, so the number of terms is q−p+1. If p=q, the sum contains only a_p. The final line connects consecutive partial sums to individual terms, with a_1=S_1 as the starting case. The student booklet's Key Ideas box remains for students to complete.
:::
